page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, fall into the average range. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in small-model LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds for a 135M model, though performance drops to the bottom 10% when executing text generation on a large 70B model.

With its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC processor, the E32as_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of top-tier single-core speeds and substantial memory capacity makes it well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks. The lack of local storage means users must rely on external Premium Storage, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
